text:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a compact 'Quality Envelope' that we attach to quant profiles. It encodes acceptable quality regressions and runtime fallback guidance. Link to RFC: https://redwood/internal/rfcs/quant-quality-envelope :point_right:
li: short question — how is this different from existing precision profiles? :thinking:
maya: profiles today mostly list op-level precisions. envelope adds behavioral thresholds (eg. loss_delta_pct, inconsistency_rate) + allowed fallback order + canary rules. Runtime reads envelope to decide instant fallbacks without running heavy evals.
zach: runtime perf concern — fine as long as checks are O(1) and data is small. we can't do per-request sampling on hot path.
maya: agreed. design: envelope is tiny (few numbers + flags). heavy stuff like shadow-eval lives asynchronously and updates the envelope. runtime uses cached envelope + short-circuit rules.
ron: per-tenant overrides worry me. sales will want to opt-in to riskier low-bit modes. how do we prevent accidental customer breakage?
maya: two guardrails: 1) envelope has a "safety_lock" enum (strict|canary|open). 2) control-plane must set override with a signed justification and ops ack. also support rollback windows.
li: can we see a sample envelope?
maya: sure — here's the minimal schema we discussed:
```json
{
  "profile_id": "fp8-v2-compact",
  "loss_delta_pct": 1.5,
  "token_coherency_drop_pct": 0.8,
  "allowed_fallback_order": ["fp8","int8","4bit","fp32"],
  "safety_lock": "canary",
  "canary_pct": 2,
  "shadow_eval_sampling": 0.01,
  "rollback_window_hours": 24
}
```
zach: ok. runtime decision would be something like: if loss_delta_pct > envelope.loss_delta_pct then try next fallback in allowed_fallback_order, else serve. keep it eager and cheap.
ron: telemetry question — what signals do we ship to make the envelope meaningful?
maya: minimal set: loss_delta_pct (vs baseline), token_coherency_drop_pct (simple n-gram OR next-token prob metric), sample_cliff_rate (for hallucinations), tail-severity (long-answer degradation). these are aggregated in 1m/5m buckets.
li: are these standardized per-model? per-route?
maya: per-profile by default, route-level overrides allowed. profiles can inherit base envelopes. control-plane resolves by precedence: tenant -> route -> global profile.
ron: sounds good but need RBAC. only SRE+Solutions can set safety_lock to open.
li: ops playbook? what do on-call do if we see regression?
maya: automatic lightweight rollback if loss_delta_pct exceeds emergency threshold (configurable), else page on-call with suggested rollback profile.
dev-bot: created issue 4621: "quality-envelope: implement runtime reader + k/v cache for envelopes"
zach: one more: fallback cost tradeoff. some fallbacks reduce latency but hurt quality, others increase latency but keep quality. envelope should allow weighting so routing can consider cost vs quality.
maya: good call. add a "cost_penalty" vector matched to each fallback in the envelope. runtime/routing can use it for smart routing.
li: wrap-up action items?
maya: actions:
- maya: write PR for profile schema + control-plane API (ETA 48h) :memo:
- zach: prototype runtime reader + O(1) short-circuit (ETA 72h) :gear:
- ron: draft RBAC + ops playbook (ETA 48h) :page_with_curl:
- li: add suggested telemetry fields to observability schema (ETA 24h) :bar_chart:
thanks everyone :rocket:
